editorNote: Quiet week on the big releases. Figma showed how it wants designers to brief its agent with Specs, and Nielsen Norman Group put evidence behind the question of whether AI can design from raw research. The other thread is control: Canva added an AI off switch after creative pushback, and Google moved Gemini users to shareable Skills.

lead.title: Workflow lab: Turning context into a plan with Specs and the Figma agent
lead.summary: Figma walks through a workflow where project context becomes a plan using Specs and its agent. It shows how the company expects designers to brief and steer the agent.
lead.whyItMatters: Try structuring your brief as a spec before handing work to an agent.

top.title: Can AI Generate Good Designs from Raw User Data?
top.author: Megan Chan, Rachel Banawa
top.summary: Nielsen Norman Group tests whether AI can produce good designs starting from raw user research data. Written by named researchers, it adds evidence to a debate that is mostly opinion.
top.whyItMatters: Shows where AI synthesis helps and where you still need to check it.

top.title: Now you can explore any idea in parallel without touching what's live
top.summary: Lovable adds a way to explore several ideas in parallel without changing the live version of a project. It targets the risk of breaking something while iterating.
top.whyItMatters: Lets you branch design explorations without touching production.

top.title: Canva added an AI ‘kill switch’ to its tools
top.author: Jesus Diaz
top.summary: Canva has added a switch that lets users turn off AI features in its tools, according to Fast Company. It responds to creative-community pushback.
top.whyItMatters: A product pattern to watch: opt-out controls for AI features.

top.title: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills – and share them
top.author: Artie Beaty
top.summary: ZDNET explains Google's new Skills, which replace Gemini Gems and can be shared. A how-to from a named writer.
top.whyItMatters: Shows packaged instructions arriving in mainstream consumer AI.

top.title: How 1Password uses Figma Make to design for trust and certainty
top.summary: Figma profiles how the 1Password team uses Figma Make in its design work. It is a vendor-published case study focused on communicating trust in the product.
top.whyItMatters: A concrete example of Make in a security-sensitive product team.
